_doc: Genre tags, one line per list. Back-end only - this file is never rendered
as a page, and no property file carries a genre. Read by tools/genrecheck.py.
WHY IT LIVES HERE (CLU-510, approved 2026-09-12). Genre is a judgement about
a whole list, not data about it, and there are 238 lists. On the property
files it would be 238 diffs to review, 238 files to rewrite to rename a
genre, and every one of those rewrites would touch shipped row ids. In one
side table keyed by slug it is one file, read top to bottom, with nothing at
stake if it is wrong. tools/data/sequences.json - the watch-prerequisite
registry - is the same shape for the same reason.
THE VOCABULARY IS CLOSED: eight genres, and a list takes 0, 1 or 2 of them.
Two is the measured cap, not a guess: with two allowed almost nothing is
misfiled, and a third tag would be honest for perhaps six lists and would
make every shelf a superset of every other.
WESTERN WAS DROPPED. Exactly two lists would carry it (deadwood, john-wayne)
and a shelf of two beside a shelf of forty-six is not a shelf. It comes back
when four lists want it. Also rejected before counting: thriller, mystery,
romance, documentary, war, animation, historical, mecha, isekai, noir, space
opera - mystery collapses into crime, animation is a medium, and the rest are
under four lists or are a medium wearing a genre's name.
WHAT 'drama' MEANS HERE, because it is the tag that would otherwise eat the
catalogue: the list's PRIMARY mode is realist character drama. It is a second
tag only where the drama is the reason people watch and something else drives
the plot - breaking-bad, the-wire, the-sopranos, battlestar-galactica, mash.
A war anime with a political spine (code-geass) or a manhunt with a sad
ending (monster) does not get it; 'has dramatic scenes' is not a genre.
AND WHAT 'action' DOES NOT MEAN: a control scheme. An action RPG, an action
platformer and an action-adventure are named for how you play them, which is
the same objection the 'mechanical' clause raises about mario - so zelda,
metroid, castlevania, mega-man, kingdom-hearts, fromsoft, resident-evil and
half-life-portal carry their content tag alone. Action IS tagged where combat,
stunts or pursuit are the spectacle on offer: martial-arts films, spy and
military thrillers, shooters, and the shonen battle series, where the fighting
is the entire proposition rather than the interface.
THE SIX EXEMPTION CLAUSES. A list with no genre must say which clause exempts
it, because 54 empty lines with no reason are indistinguishable from 54 lines
nobody got to. tools/genrecheck.py enforces that.
person     - one person's body of work. Kubrick is not a genre. A person
list DOES take a tag where the whole body of work is one genre
and saying so is not a stretch (bruce-lee, carpenter,
agatha-christie); those lines are marked PERSON, TAGGED.
canon      - an award, a poll, a national canon, an archive, a reception
category. It selects for quality or provenance, not content.
device     - a formal constraint: one room, one clock, one cut, one day
repeating. Members span every genre by design.
studio     - a studio, imprint or licensing line. A slate is not a genre.
mechanical - the word people use for its genre names a mechanic, not a
story (platformer, immersive sim).
gated      - the password list, which is not described in this repo.
THE NOTE CONVENTION. A note is a sibling key: the slug with '?' on the end,
on the line directly under the tags it explains. Notes are for anything not
obvious - every exemption, every close call - and are deliberately absent
where the answer is not in doubt (star-trek is sci-fi). A note starting
AMBIGUOUS is a call that could reasonably go the other way, and it says which
way and what the argument is, so it can be overruled in one pass without
reopening the reasoning.
TO ADD A LIST: put its slug in "lists" with its tags, or with [] and a note
starting 'EXEMPT <clause>'. tools/genrecheck.py fails if you skip it, so an
untagged list cannot arrive quietly - which is the entire point of the file.
A slug here with no property file fails too, unless its note starts PENDING.
Genre shelves that exist, as slug -> the genre (and optionally the medium)
the shelf is meant to be complete for. tools/genrecheck.py prints which
lists carry that genre and are not a door on the shelf - the same hint
build.py prints for Directors and Marvel Comics, and the reason this file
exists at all. A shelf named here with no property file yet is skipped with
a line saying so, so the entry can be written before the shelf is built.
Hints, never failures: whether a candidate belongs is curation.

sitcoms._why: CLU-532. The comedy lists with television in them, with a British sitcoms section. Built separately; this line is the net under it.

lists.a24?: EXEMPT studio - a slate, not a genre: A24 puts out horror, comedy and drama in the same year.
lists.ace-attorney?: Courtroom mystery. Comedy is its tone, not its genre, so one tag.
lists.agatha-christie?: PERSON, TAGGED - eighty-five novels and every one of them a crime novel.
lists.archer?: Spy comedy, one tag: the action is parodied rather than delivered.
lists.attack-on-titan?: AMBIGUOUS fantasy vs sci-fi. The titans eventually get an engineered, biological explanation, but the mode is dark fantasy for most of the run. Filed fantasy.
lists.bad-movie-night?: EXEMPT canon - a reception category. Being bad is not a genre.
lists.batman?: AMBIGUOUS superhero vs crime. Batman is a detective and this reading order is thick with crime stories. One tag anyway: if every masked vigilante is crime, the crime shelf becomes a subset of the superhero one.
lists.battlestar-galactica?: Both load-bearing: a war drama that happens to be aboard spaceships.
lists.best-directors-cuts?: EXEMPT device - a list about which VERSION of a film to watch, spanning every genre.
lists.best-picture?: EXEMPT canon - an award, 621 nominees deep.
lists.black-mirror?: One tag. Several episodes play as horror, but the engine is always technology and no two episodes share a world.
lists.body-swap?: EXEMPT device - a premise. The 69 films include comedies, horror and one thriller.
lists.bottle-episodes?: EXEMPT device - a production constraint, one episode at a time, across 32 shows of every kind.
lists.bruce-lee?: PERSON, TAGGED - martial arts from the child roles on.
lists.cardcaptor-sakura?: Magical girl, filed fantasy, one tag. No action: the fights are not the appeal and a magical-girl show on an action shelf reads wrong.
lists.carpenter?: PERSON, TAGGED - horror, and the exceptions are horror-shaped.
lists.cates-venom?: AMBIGUOUS. Cates writes Venom as cosmic horror, and horror would be the second tag if it had one. Filed superhero alone because it is a Marvel ongoing about a Spider-Man character.
lists.chuck?: Spy action-comedy, and unlike archer it delivers both.
lists.code-geass?: Mecha war with a heavy political spine. One tag - see what 'drama' means, in _doc.
lists.criterion?: EXEMPT canon - an archive of 1,337 spine numbers.
lists.cronenberg?: PERSON, TAGGED - body horror is the whole filmography, including the films not sold as horror.
lists.cult-classics?: EXEMPT canon - a reception category: 326 films that 3 of 23 reference works call cult.
lists.daredevil?: AMBIGUOUS, and both tags are deliberate. Miller, Bendis, Brubaker and Zdarsky write crime fiction in a costume - this is the one superhero list where crime is the story rather than the setting. Overrule it and batman follows.
lists.deadwood?: Would be western, which the vocabulary drops. Drama is what is left, and it is honest: this is a prestige character drama with hats.
lists.death-note?: AMBIGUOUS crime vs fantasy - a detective duel with a death god in the room. Filed crime: the investigation is the engine and the supernatural is one rule.
lists.directors?: EXEMPT person - the hub of 15 filmographies, every one exempt for the same reason.
lists.discworld?: Both load-bearing: comic fantasy is the entire proposition.
lists.disney?: EXEMPT studio - 652 films with nothing in common but the logo.
lists.doctor-who?: AMBIGUOUS, flagged in advance - sci-fi by premise, anything at all by episode: historical, horror, farce. Filed sci-fi because the show is about a time machine.
lists.donnie-yen?: PERSON, TAGGED - action, and credited with the action on 27 of them.
lists.eastwood?: EXEMPT person - and the near-miss the clause exists for. Westerns and Dirty Harry put him close to two genres, one of which the vocabulary drops. Untagged is the safe direction.
lists.final-fantasy?: Filed fantasy across the whole numbered line even though VII, VIII and XIII are science fiction with swords - the franchise is shelved as fantasy everywhere else, including on its own box.
lists.flcl?: AMBIGUOUS - a coming-of-age story with robots and a guitar. Both tags are half-true and neither is true alone.
lists.fps-canon?: Tagged where immersive is exempt, and the difference is the one in the mechanical clause: an immersive sim is a design philosophy whose members are set in any world at all, while a shooter is 27 games about shooting people. The content is the action.
lists.fromsoft?: Dark fantasy. No action tag: 'action RPG' names how you hold the controller, not what the game is about - see the mechanical-action rule in _doc. Bloodborne is horror and the adjacents include science fiction; neither is enough of the ten to move the tag.
lists.ghibli?: EXEMPT studio - and the clearest case for the clause: Totoro, Grave of the Fireflies and Porco Rosso share a studio and nothing else.
lists.gilmore-girls?: AMBIGUOUS - an hour-long comedy-drama, and one of the few where drama comes first. Tagging comedy means a sitcom shelf will offer it; refusing it there is the shelf's curation, not this file's job.
lists.godzilla?: AMBIGUOUS, flagged in advance. Kaiju is its own genre and there is no room for it. 1954 is horror, the Showa middle is children's adventure, Shin is a procedural. Filed for both ends and honestly neither.
lists.half-life-portal?: One tag for both lines: Half-Life is a shooter and Portal a puzzle game, and what they share is the universe, not the verb.
lists.hawks?: EXEMPT person - gangsters, screwball, noir and westerns from one man across 44 years. The clause and the reality agree.
lists.hellboy?: AMBIGUOUS - filed horror + fantasy rather than superhero, because the Mignolaverse is folklore and occult detection rather than capes. It is a comics list with no superhero tag, which is the unusual part.
lists.hitchcock?: EXEMPT person - close to one genre, the thriller, which the vocabulary does not carry. Untagged is the safe direction.
lists.immersive?: EXEMPT mechanical, flagged in advance - an immersive sim is a design philosophy, and its 23 members are set in cyberpunk, horror and fantasy worlds alike.
lists.indie-essentials?: EXEMPT canon - a house canon selected by how the games were funded.
lists.jackass?: Comedy, and it has television in its media, so a comedy shelf will offer it. It is not a sitcom; see gilmore-girls.
lists.jackie-chan?: PERSON, TAGGED - action across 155 films and 64 years.
lists.japanese-cinema?: EXEMPT canon - a national canon picked by a magazine and its juries.
lists.john-wayne?: EXEMPT person - and the one list whose genre is unarguable and unavailable: western, dropped for having only two members.
lists.kill-la-kill?: AMBIGUOUS - absurdist action on an alien-fibre premise. One tag: the comedy is tonal and the science fiction is a MacGuffin.
lists.kubrick?: EXEMPT person - the clause's own example: roughly one film per genre, deliberately.
lists.lego-games?: EXEMPT studio - a licensing line. Every genre appears, wearing bricks.
lists.lost?: AMBIGUOUS, flagged in advance - a mystery for five seasons and science fiction for two, and mystery is not in the vocabulary. Both tags, drama first.
lists.mario?: EXEMPT mechanical, flagged in advance - a platformer. What narrative it has is one kidnapping repeated nineteen times, and that is nobody's genre.
lists.mash?: Both load-bearing: the show that invented the modern comedy-drama, and half its famous episodes are not funny.
lists.mega-man?: AMBIGUOUS against mario, which is exempt as mechanical. Tagged sci-fi because it has a narrative premise - robots, a mad scientist, ninety-four games about them - where Mario has only a mechanic. No action tag: it is a platformer. If that distinction is too fine, exempt this as mechanical too.
lists.monster?: A manhunt for a serial killer. One tag - see what 'drama' means, in _doc.
lists.mst3k?: Comedy: the riffing is the show, and the films being riffed are somebody else's genre.
lists.nathan-fielder?: PERSON, TAGGED - comedy, of a kind nobody else makes.
lists.one-location-films?: EXEMPT device - a constraint on the set.
lists.one-punch-man?: Both load-bearing: a parody only works if it is also the thing.
lists.persona?: AMBIGUOUS - urban fantasy over a school calendar. Filed fantasy; the alternative is no tag, because the genre people name when they talk about Persona is 'JRPG', which is mechanical.
lists.pokemon?: AMBIGUOUS - a fantasy world explained with machines. One tag, fantasy.
lists.psych?: Both load-bearing: a case-of-the-week procedural that is a comedy first.
lists.raimi?: PERSON, TAGGED - horror, and three Spider-Man films are the reason this is a call rather than a fact. Exempting it instead is reasonable.
lists.real-time-films?: EXEMPT device - a constraint on the clock.
lists.ridley-scott?: EXEMPT person - Alien, Thelma & Louise and Gladiator, from one man.
lists.sailor-moon?: Magical girl, filed fantasy, one tag - the same call as cardcaptor-sakura.
lists.samurai-jack?: AMBIGUOUS - a samurai stranded in a robot future by a shape-shifting demon. Filed action + fantasy; sci-fi has an equal claim on it.
lists.satoshi-kon?: EXEMPT person - four films close to the psychological thriller, which the vocabulary does not carry.
lists.scorsese?: EXEMPT person - and the near-miss worth naming, because half of it is crime. Untagged for the same reason as eastwood.
lists.sight-and-sound?: EXEMPT canon - a critics' poll, as ranked.
lists.sitcoms?: The comedy shelf itself (CLU-532), which is a box set of comedy lists. Tagged comedy so it is not an untagged list; genrecheck never asks a shelf to be a door on itself.
lists.spawn?: Both load-bearing: a hellspawn antihero in a nineties cape book.
lists.star-wars?: AMBIGUOUS, flagged in advance. It is a fantasy with spaceships - a wizard, a sword, a farm boy, a princess. Filed sci-fi alone because that is where everyone looks for it. Adding fantasy as the second tag is the one-word change if you disagree.
lists.stephen-king?: PERSON, TAGGED - horror, with the Dark Tower and the prison books as the exceptions that prove it.
lists.suda51?: EXEMPT person - one designer's credit list, spanning Super Famicom wrestling, visual novels and an assassin comedy. Action would be a guess about half of it.
lists.tarantino?: EXEMPT person - and a second near-miss: crime for four of the ten, war for two, western for two.
lists.the-big-o?: Mecha noir. One tag; crime would be the second and the detective work is thin.
lists.time-loops?: EXEMPT device - one premise held by comedies, horror films, whole sitcom seasons and a Star Trek episode.
lists.tremors?: AMBIGUOUS - the 1990 film is comedy-horror and six of the sequels are not. One tag on purpose: tagging it comedy would offer a creature feature to a sitcom shelf, because it has a television series in it.
lists.twin-peaks?: AMBIGUOUS - a murder investigation, a small-town melodrama and whatever the Black Lodge is, and only two tags fit. Crime is the one dropped: the murder is solved halfway through season two and the show carries on.
lists.vampire-diaries?: AMBIGUOUS - a teen melodrama with vampires. Filed fantasy + drama rather than horror, because nothing in it is trying to frighten anyone.
lists.vertigo?: EXEMPT studio - an imprint, and its three runs are a western-horror, a satire and a post-apocalypse.
lists.vinland-saga?: AMBIGUOUS - a historical Viking story whose second season is largely about farming. Historical is not in the vocabulary, and action + drama is the closest honest pair.
lists.x-files?: AMBIGUOUS, flagged in advance - science fiction and horror by turns, with a comedy run in the middle. Both tags; comedy is what does not fit in two.
